truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 identified 11 findings covering 7 of the 20 true vulnerabilities (SC-V3-001, 004, 006, 009, 010, 011, 020 fully; SC-V3-013 partially). Twelve true vulnerabilities were missed entirely. All Run 2 findings were supported by the source code with no false positives. A consistent pattern of severity underclaiming was observed across all matched vulnerabilities.

Items.Notes: Run 2 finding 1 exactly matches the anchor pattern: runtime_log_format() returns a user-controllable format string passed directly to printf. Severity (Critical) and CWE (CWE-134) both match.
Run 2 contains no finding related to integer overflow in the factorial computation (lines 312-320, result *= i with long long). The factorial function lacks overflow detection.

Run 2 contains no finding for the use-after-free in stage_deferred_history_flush where scratch allocated from g_memory_pool is used in a thread-pool lambda after memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() frees it in cleanup().
Run 2 finding 5 exactly matches the anchor pattern. However, severity was underclaimed: Run 2 reported High while the true severity is Critical.

Run 2 contains no finding for the stack buffer overflow at lines 831-832 where strcpy(input_buffer_, expression.c_str()) is called when expression.length() >= sizeof(input_buffer_), bypassing the safe_string_copy guard.
Run 2 finding 8 exactly matches the anchor pattern. The race condition (read before lock) is correctly identified. Severity was underclaimed: Run 2 reported Low vs. true Medium.
Run 2 contains no finding for the logic bomb in authenticate() where login_attempts_ > 5 combined with EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE bypasses authentication (lines 592-598).
Run 2 contains no finding for path traversal in ConfigLoader::load_config where config_dir_ + filename concatenates user input without sanitization (line 543).
Run 2 finding 3 exactly matches the anchor pattern. Heap overflow via unchecked strcpy into a 256-byte pooled buffer. Severity was underclaimed: Run 2 reported High vs. true Critical.
Run 2 finding 7 exactly matches the anchor pattern. Hardcoded admin credential correctly identified. Severity was underclaimed: Run 2 reported Medium vs. true High.
Run 2 finding 9 exactly matches the anchor pattern. Weak PRNG producing only 4-digit tokens correctly identified. Severity was underclaimed: Run 2 reported Low vs. true High.
Run 2 contains no finding for the thread-unsafe static std::tm cached_time combined with localtime() at lines 230-231, which is not thread-safe and lacks synchronization.

Run 2 finding 6 identified the command injection aspect of this code path (CWE-78) but did not separately identify the insecure temporary file handling vulnerability (CWE-377). The TEMP/TMPDIR-based path construction and use of system() with shell redirection are present, but the classification and CWE differ from the true vulnerability.
Run 2 contains no finding for persistent authentication state (authenticated_, login_attempts_, session_token_) lacking timeout or logout mechanism (lines 578-584).
Run 2 contains no finding for the unhandled exception risk in std::stod(tokens[3]) at line 729 within handle_variable_command, which can throw std::invalid_argument or std::out_of_range.

Run 2 contains no finding for the integer underflow in MemoryPool::allocate at lines 132-133 where size_t remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES; can underflow when previous_size - size < 64.

Run 2 contains no finding for unbounded recursion in parse_expression → parse_factor → parse_expression via PAREN_OPEN at lines 426-430, with no depth limit enforcement despite MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH existing in config.
Run 2 contains no finding for the data race in ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached where result_cache_ is accessed without holding cache_mutex_ (lines 445-451), despite the mutex being declared.

Run 2 contains no finding for the TOCTOU race in ConfigLoader::load_config between std::filesystem::exists (line 544) and std::ifstream file (line 546), exacerbated by the intentional sleep_for delay at line 545.
Run 2 finding 10 exactly matches the anchor pattern. Division by zero when token_length is 0 is correctly identified. Severity (Low) and CWE (CWE-369) both match.
